notes: max_critical is 2, and CSC-VTY-0001 and CSC-MGT-0010 are both in must_fire, matching the real ruleset. This fixture configures `line vty 0 4` with `transport input ssh` (compliant), but never mentions `vty 5 15`; that sub-range is assumed (CSC-SELF-0006 fires) and evaluated against the platform default, per the rule that a check passes only when every returned range passes. The IOS-XE default vty transport is not SSH-only, so CSC-VTY-0001 ('A vty line accepts a non-SSH transport') correctly fires at `critical` on the assumed 5-15 range even though 0-4 is hardened. max_high is 21 (the real count, 16, plus a small headroom): this trap fixture exercises implicit defaults broadly, so many families' absence checks fire on a minimal config. This fixture also has no `version` line: with no version line, iosxe is treated as having vstack ON as a fail-safe, since an ambiguous or 3.x version cannot prove Smart Install is safely absent, unless `no vstack` is present -- which this fixture correctly does not have -- so CSC-MGT-0010 also correctly fires as critical. This is not fixed by adding a version line or `no vstack`: the no-version case is exactly what the fail-safe exists to catch.
